title: Model Version Explorer & Publish Controls for Console
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: Customers struggle to understand which model version is active for a route and which published performance profile will be used at inference time. Current console lacks a single place to explore model versions, pin a version to a route, and publish/view performance profiles (latency/cost/accuracy trade-offs).

Goal: Build a Model Version Explorer in Console that: 1) surfaces available model variants and historical model releases, 2) allows explicit version pinning at route and deployment scope, 3) enables publishing and previewing performance profiles (P50/P95 latency, tokens/sec, estimated cost per 1k tokens, memory footprint, recommended quantization), and 4) integrates with rollouts (canary/A-B) and fallback policies so engineers can reason about effective runtime behavior.

Scope: UI + product flow for model selection and profile publishing in Console. Includes read/write pinning controls, profile compare view, and a quick validation step that simulates cost/latency impact against a sample probe workload.

Out of scope: Deep runtime changes for routing/fallback implementation (handled in ENG tickets), advanced per-tenant RBAC controls (separate security epic).
acceptance_criteria: Console has a Model Version Explorer page listing models + versions with sortable columns: version tag, release date, profile summary (latency/cost), and compatibility flags.
Users can pin a specific model version to a route or environment and see immediate confirmation of effective model for that route, including any fallback behavior.

Admins can publish a performance profile for a model version with fields: P50 latency, P95 latency, median tokens/sec, estimated cost/1k, and notes. Published profiles are visible on the version detail pane.
A compare mode lets users select two versions/profiles and see side-by-side differences and an estimated impact calculator that uses historical route traffic distribution (if available).
Pin/unpin actions are audited and produce a changelog entry with user, timestamp, and optional reason note.
Rollout controls allow creating a canary split (eg. 5% traffic) targeting a pinned version and show previewed metrics and alerting thresholds before activation.
Design handoff artifacts (Figma screens + interaction specs) are attached and reviewed; ENG has created stub endpoints for pinning and profile publish in ENG-2895.
comments: 2026-02-28 Aisha Patel: Initial ticket created after product review with Growth and Platform. Primary user need: reduce surprises when a model upgrade changes latency/cost profiles. Attached early PRD and success metrics.

2026-03-01 Marcus Liu: Met with Design (DES-4301) and Engineering (ENG-2895). Agreed on a unified Explorer page rather than sprinkling controls across route pages. Trade-off: slight longer path to pin from route page, but much better discoverability and auditability.

2026-03-02 Mei Chen (Design): Shared three Figma variants for the Explorer: timeline-first, table-first, and card-comparison. We favored table-first for scale with an optional timeline drawer. Designer notes attached in links.

2026-03-03 Rahul Singh (Eng): Estimated backend work ~ 3 pts to add profile publish endpoints and 2 pts for pin API. ENG-2895 will surface current effective model per route; ENG-3172 will handle audit logs. We flagged a potential race when pinning during an ongoing rollout — eng to propose guardrails.

2026-03-04 Marcus Liu: Decided on UX for pin confirmation modal: must show current active model, proposed pinned model, and fallbacks with a 2-step confirm + optional reason. This simplifies rollback auditing. Design to add mockups for modal and rollout split selector.

2026-03-05 Aisha Patel: Added acceptance criteria for compare mode and estimated impact calculator. Requested that the profile publish UI include an optional sample inference probe that runs against a chosen test prompt set (non-blocking; will be async and show status).
